record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: For a conducting sequence beta in {0,1}*, which words u can be shuffled with themselves to obtain a unique square-free word?

evidence.quote: Which words u can be shuffled to obtain a unique square-free word u  beta u?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. A word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is called square-free if it contains no nonempty factor of the form $xx$ (i.e., no nonempty word repeated twice consecutively appears as a contiguous block of $w$).

For two words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$ of lengths $m$ and $n$ respectively, and a binary "conducting sequence" $\beta \in \{0,1\}^{m+n}$ containing exactly $m$ zeros and $n$ ones, the shuffle of $u$ and $v$ controlled by $\beta$, denoted $u \shuffle_\beta v$, is the unique word of length $m+n$ obtained by reading the $i$-th letter from $u$ when the $i$-th symbol of $\beta$ is $0$ (in order) and from $v$ when it is $1$ (in order).

Define a self-shuffle of $u$ as any word of the form $u \shuffle_\beta u$ where $\beta \in \{0,1\}^{2|u|}$ has exactly $|u|$ zeros and $|u|$ ones.

Problem: Characterize all words $u \in \Sigma^*$ for which there exists a conducting sequence $\beta$ such that $u \shuffle_\beta u$ is square-free, and moreover such a square-free self-shuffle is unique (i.e., $u \shuffle_\beta u$ is square-free for exactly one $\beta$).
artifact.status_search_result: Related questions on square-free shuffles and self-shuffling have been studied: it is known (Harju and others) that there exist infinite square-free words that are self-shuffling, and recent work shows arbitrarily long shuffled-square-free words exist over alphabets of size ≥ 6, while recognition of shuffled-square-free words is NP-complete. However, no source directly resolves the specific question of characterizing words u admitting a unique square-free self-shuffle u ⧢_β u, so the status appears to be unresolved/unknown.

status_evidence.title: On shuffled-square-free words
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of arbitrarily long shuffled-square-free words on 6+ letter alphabets; recognizing shuffled-square-free words is NP-complete.
status_evidence.claim: Related progress on shuffled-square-free words exists, but does not characterize words with unique square-free self-shuffles.

status_evidence.title: Infinite square-free self-shuffling words
status_evidence.snippet: There exists an infinite square-free word u on three letters such that u can be shuffled with itself to produce another infinite square-free word.
status_evidence.claim: A related existence question (Harju's question) has been answered, but uniqueness characterization is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Square-Free Shuffles of Words
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which pairs of words can be shuffled into a square-free word.
status_evidence.claim: General shuffle-to-square-free questions are studied; specific uniqueness question for self-shuffles not directly resolved.
